newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says tankan result in line with its assessment.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says tankan result in line with its assessment.

text.p: The result of the June "tankan" corporate survey was in line with the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) assessment of Japan's economic recovery, Masayuki Matsushima, director of the central bank's Research and Statistics Department, told a news conference on Wednesday.

Asked whether the tankan result, released earlier on Wednesday, matched the BOJ's assessment of the economy, Matsushima said: "Overall it (the survey result) shows a movement in line with (our assessment)."

He also said the result showed that a positive mechanism within the economy that was showing an improvement in production, private incomes and corporate earnings was also firm in the corporate sector.
Matsushima added that it was difficult to make an overall judgment of the economy based on the tankan alone.
He said a significant improvement in business sentiment among major manufacturers was backed by a rise in exports and also a strong performance in the telecommunications sector.
Although sentiment among major non-manufacturers was dampened due to the rise in the consumption tax in April, their outlook was expected to improve in the future, he said.

As for smaller firms, he said sentiment among manufacturers was mixed and was largely unchanged from the March survey, but among non-manufacturers sentiment worsened as a drop in public works spending had hurt the construction sector.
Matsushima also said the recent correction of the yen's weakness did not appear to have had a major impact on overall corporate sentiment.

He said that while sentiment in some industries, such as the oil industry, might be affected by recent foreign exchange fluctuations, "the recent foreign exchange levels are not something that will affect the business outlook of firms (overall)".
Asked about the impact of April's consumption tax increase, Matsushima said sentiment of big non-manufacturers had been affected.
He added that while some impact may be seen in large manufacturers' sentiment, once the effects of the tax increase tapered off sentiment would recover.
Matsushima also said exports may temporarily increase in the first half of fiscal 1997/98, but the overall trend would be towards a decline.
